title: Pictograms / Gradient treatments — Dark background

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: Dark background

slide_intent: Use a controlled gradient to enrich simple linework, because a consistent color transition can add character without introducing unrelated effects.
strategic_value: Related two-color gradients can give IBM’s varied pictogram concepts a shared luminous treatment on dark fields.
demonstration: Eight outlined pictograms form two rows on near-black, including an exit arrow, wheelchair, globe, racket, overlapping squares, rocket, network and bandage.
practical_value: Choose a permitted two-color gradient while keeping the pictogram silhouette legible against the dark field.

content_islands.name: Background selector
content_islands.spec: Show Dark background selected above the examples.

content_islands.name: Upper gradient row
content_islands.spec: Align exit, accessibility, globe and racket symbols with cyan/blue, green/teal and purple/magenta transitions.

content_islands.name: Lower gradient row
content_islands.spec: Continue with overlapping squares, rocket, connected circles and bandage examples.

reference_purposes.Expression: Colored transitions enrich the same thin-line pictogram structure across eight concepts.
reference_purposes.Application: The specimens show gradient pictograms on a dark field.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying gradient section specifies accepted two-color families and 45° application; it rejects radial gradients, more than two colors and blends more than two palette steps apart.
